title: Is it just me or is it hard for everyone?
author: chaylarian

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Is the title engagement bait?

Anyway gamedev is especially hard for people who go straight to vibe coding without learning any gamedev.

replies.author: chaylarian
replies.body:
More of a joke than engagement bait actually

My first game was aimed at children and was intentionally much simpler. Then I started working on combat mechanics, got carried away, and somehow ended up making a much faster and harder action game.

replies.author: Exp5000
replies.body: There's two types of AI users. Those who have zero clue how to ask questions and just willy nilly build garbage. Then there's those who realize AI can teach you everything it's making as it's making things. I recently learned not everyone is the second person and it brings me joy to know even with AI people lack curiosity. That's more sad than AI taking jobs. Imagine building something and not think "how does that actually work now that it's built".

replies.author: chaylarian
replies.body: Spot on. Using it as a mentor to understand the *w*hy behind the code is a game-changer. Thanks for the support!

replies.author: ollieschmolly
replies.body: This is a very critical topic. So much of the incredible case of AI is that it can help you understand the system and then you and the AI can work to make it better. Keep building!

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: There's also the third category that are already good at a job, then use AI to enhance their skills or speed up the work tremendously.

replies.author: Exp5000
replies.body: Yeah absolutely, I'd still say that falls under person number 2. Someone who knows how things work and is still actively learning as they go. When does one ever stop learning?

replies.author: mallcopsarebastards
replies.body: I'm neither of those people. I'm a professional developer with 20 years experience. I use claude code to accelerate my process, but I apply project skills like how to plan and architect, how to unit test, how to refactor systems rather than bolting on functionality.

replies.author: Exp5000
replies.body: Yeah sorry I don't have time to sit here and actually paint the reality of an extremely nuanced hobby. I'd say you fall under number two of my generalization. I'll follow up with a No shit Sherlock.

replies.author: godver3
replies.body: It is 100% engagement bait. The whole thing is - it's just a crappy ad.

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596

replies.author: chaylarian
replies.body: The ultimate gamedev checklist 😃 It's tough, but you'll get the hang of it, I promise!
